_comment: colorburst disk layout. Identical to reven's (disk_layout_v2) except for
the OEM partition, #8.
#8 holds the colorburst variant configuration -- the one file that says
which language and, in time, which behaviour this device has. It is the
only partition that survives all three of install (chromeos-install copies
it USB -> disk), OTA (payloads carry KERN + ROOT only) and powerwash
(clobber_state wipes STATE), and it carries neither a dm-verity hash tree
nor a signature, so writing to it neither needs a rebuild nor invalidates
anything.
It is FAT32 rather than ext4 so that the person preparing a USB stick can
open colorburst.txt in Notepad. That is the whole reason: the people who
hand a laptop to a relative are on Windows, and telling them to boot Linux
to change the language would defeat the point of making language a file.
Windows also needs the partition TYPE to be Microsoft basic data, which is
not expressible here -- chromite's VALID_PARTITION_TYPES has no such entry
-- so release/make-variant.sh sets that GUID after the build.
64 MiB, up from the stock 16 MiB, because FAT32 requires at least 65525
clusters and 16 MiB yields 32224. mkfs.vfat builds that undersized
filesystem without complaint -- only fsck.vfat says 'less than the required
minimum ... may lead to problems on some systems' -- and an out-of-spec
FAT32 is exactly the thing Windows may balk at, which would defeat the
point. 64 MiB gives ~129k clusters, comfortably in spec, and leaves room
for whatever a variant needs to carry later.
fs_format is 'vfat', NOT 'fat32', with the FAT32 asked for via fs_options.
The same string is used for two different things: filesystem_util.sh takes
it as an mkfs selector, where 'fat32' means mkfs.vfat -F 32, but it is also
baked into the image as FS_FORMAT_OEM and handed STRAIGHT to mount(2) by
chromeos_startup (init/startup/stateful_mount.cc). 'fat32' is not a kernel
filesystem name, so that mount fails with ENODEV, /usr/share/oem stays
empty, and every device silently falls back to English. Found by booting
it: 'mount of /usr/share/oem failed with code 0: No such device (19)'.
'vfat' satisfies both readers and still mounts FAT12/16/32 alike.
The override lives in 'common' so every image type inherits it; 'base' is
present but empty because chromite requires the key to exist.
